name: cpu_video_decode

license.notes: Task source stays source-available; openh264 is BSD-2-Clause (permissive), so linking it imposes no copyleft. Caveat: H.264/AVC is patent-encumbered — Cisco's royalty coverage applies only to their official prebuilt openh264 binaries, so this from-source build is for evaluation/benchmark use, consistent with the repo's source-available-for-evaluation model.

libraries.name: openh264
libraries.usage: Decodes the bundled/synthesized H.264 Annex-B stream; the multi-instance decode loop is the measured workload (its encoder is used only to synthesize the stand-in stream when no clip is bundled).
libraries.notes: Built as a static library from the pinned submodule; no source modifications.

title: Software video decoding
short_description: H.264 software decode of a bundled 1080p clip on the processor.

structured_text.description: Decodes a bundled 1080p H.264 clip to raw frames entirely on the processor, with hardware decode disabled on purpose so the test measures the CPU rather than a fixed-function media engine. The clip and settings are identical on every machine. Software decoding is what runs when a codec, container or platform is not hardware-accelerated, and it is the path multi-stream editing and analytics pipelines fall back to.
structured_text.metric_explanation: The score is the average number of frames decoded per second across the clip, reported in fps.
structured_text.value_interpretation: Higher is better. More frames per second means smoother playback and scrubbing, more simultaneous streams, and faster frame extraction for downstream processing.
structured_text.reasoning: Decoding is far more common than encoding: every playback, timeline scrub, transcode front-end and video-analytics data loader runs it, which makes software decode throughput a broadly relevant real-world CPU test.

domain_gaming.explanation: Cutscenes and streamed video are decoded during play.

domain_office.explanation: Meeting recordings and embedded presentation video are decoded for playback.

domain_software_development.explanation: Developers decode video mainly when building media tooling.

domain_graphics_design.explanation: Reference footage and video assets are decoded while designing.

domain_video_editing.explanation: Smooth multi-stream playback and scrubbing on the timeline depend directly on decode speed.

domain_3d_rendering.explanation: Video textures and reference plates are decoded during production.

domain_audio_production.explanation: Scoring to picture requires decoding the video track.

domain_scientific_computing.explanation: Decoding is a minor step in most scientific pipelines.

domain_ai_training.explanation: Video-dataset data loaders decode frames on the CPU, often a training bottleneck.

domain_ai_inference.explanation: Video-analytics inference decodes input streams before the model runs.

domain_data_science.explanation: Video is decoded when it appears as a data source for analysis.

domain_server_virt.explanation: Transcoding and streaming servers decode continuously, falling back to software when the media engine is saturated or unsupported.
